title: Sell Mineral Rights in Halliday, ND
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Halliday, ND
metaDescription: Halliday sits in southeastern Dunn County near the Golden Valley line. See what that position means for your family's Bakken mineral interest.
heroLead: Halliday sits toward the southeastern edge of Dunn County, close enough to the Golden Valley County line that development here has run a bit lighter than the busiest interior of the county.
intro: Still, Dunn County as a whole is core Bakken territory, and Halliday-area tracts have seen real drilling activity even if not at the density found closer to Killdeer. Families here typically hold interests tied to early-1900s homestead patents, and confirming exactly what those patents have turned into today requires checking the current record rather than relying on memory.

sections.heading: Halliday's Position on the County's Southern Edge
paragraphs: Because Halliday sits closer to the Golden Valley County line than to Dunn County's busiest core near Killdeer, spacing units here have generally seen somewhat lighter development, though the area remains within the broader core Bakken trend rather than true flank territory.

sections.heading: What Ownership Near Halliday Typically Involves
paragraphs: Original patents in this part of Dunn County date largely to the early 1900s homestead era, and fractions have split across multiple generations of heirs since, a pattern consistent with most of rural Dunn County.

sections.heading: Where to Verify Your Halliday Mineral Record
paragraphs: The Dunn County Recorder's office in Manning holds the deed chain needed to confirm your current fraction. We pull and review that record for owners at no cost before any conversation about a lease or sale.

sections.heading: What We Check Before Talking Numbers
paragraphs: Before discussing any offer on a Halliday-area interest, we confirm current lease status, whether the tract sits inside a spacing unit, and how any nearby wells are performing, since a fair number depends on those specifics rather than a generic county-wide estimate. That review is free and comes with no obligation to move forward.

faqs.question: Is Halliday in the same drilling density as Killdeer?
faqs.answer: Generally lighter. Halliday sits closer to the Golden Valley County line, and development in this part of Dunn County has run somewhat less dense than the busier core near Killdeer.

faqs.question: Is Halliday still considered core Bakken?
faqs.answer: Yes, it remains within Dunn County's broader core Bakken trend, just on the lighter-development side of that core rather than true flank territory.

faqs.question: How do I trace my Halliday mineral interest?
faqs.answer: Start with the Dunn County Recorder's office in Manning, which holds deed and probate records tracing back to the original homestead patent in most cases.

faqs.question: Why do so many Halliday-area interests have multiple heirs listed?
faqs.answer: Original early-1900s homestead patents have typically split across several generations by now, which is standard across rural Dunn County.

faqs.question: How long has oil activity existed near Halliday?
faqs.answer: Dunn County's broader Bakken development dates to the mid-2000s, though this southeastern part of the county has generally seen somewhat lighter activity than the busier core near Killdeer.
